customManagers.description: Images pinned inside HelmRelease values, which no built-in manager reads. Annotate the line above the tag with `# renovate: datasource=docker depName=<image>`.

Full image references under an `imageName:` or `reference:` key, as CNPG's Cluster CR uses for the instance image and for each `postgresql.extensions[].image`. The built-in kubernetes manager only reads `image:`, and the tag-only manager above cannot split a repository from its tag. Annotate the line above with `# renovate: datasource=docker`.

packageRules.description: Charts from an OCI HelmRepository via chart.spec. chart.spec.version cannot carry a digest, so the `version@sha256:...` pin best-practices proposes would break the HelmRelease.
Platform and infrastructure: one PR per component (its chart plus the images pinned beside it), never merged automatically.
Flux's own controllers and CLI move together.
router/ and openstack/ providers, one PR, never merged automatically.

Apps: every non-major update in one PR, merged automatically once it is 3 days old and checks pass. A branch only automerges if every update in it does, so the rules below that hold something for review must also move it out of this group.
A pre-1.0 minor is a breaking release by semver: held for review, one PR per app.

Critical apps are never merged automatically: they gate other things (authentik, registry, woodpecker), hold data nothing regenerates (vaultwarden, immich, paperless, dawarich, stalwart, rustfs), or put breaking changes in calver minors (home-assistant, esphome). One PR per app.

The vendored cnmsql instance catalog (flux/platform/cnmsql/catalogs). Its tags are `<version>-<build time>-bookworm`; under docker versioning the build time reads as a fixed suffix and nothing would ever update, so the timestamp is the `build` component here. The moving tags (`8.4`, `8.4.11-bookworm`) and the distroless images do not match and are ignored.
A catalog entry is a series (8.0, 8.4, 9.7): moving one to another minor or major would be a major-version upgrade of every Cluster on it, so only patch and build updates are proposed.

Substrate follows kagent, not its own releases. Its version is whatever kagent's go.mod pins (`replace github.com/agent-substrate/substrate => github.com/kagent-dev/substrate <version>`), because the kagent controller is a substrate API client and substrate changes its protos between pre-releases. Bumped on its own, 0.3 -> 0.6 failed every time and left the release in a rollback loop for two weeks. Move these by hand with a kagent bump; see flux/platform/substrate/ocirepository.yaml.

kagent's chart, CRD chart and images must land together, and a pre-1.0 bump can change the database contract (see flux/platform/kagent/release.yaml) - one PR to review, not three to merge in the wrong order.
